sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Addl. SPP. for the respondent No.1 - State.
The notice issued to respondent No.2 though served, but un-represented.

03. The case of the prosecution is that on the complaint of respondent No.2, the police have registered the FIR on 23.06.2022, against 05 persons and finally filed the charge-sheet only against this petitioner, wherein it is stated that the daughter of the complainant aged about 16 years was found missing from 21.06.2022 at about 06.30 p.m. and later they came to know that the petitioner Hanamanth vs The State And Anr on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189903013/
2 was abducted her in his motorcycle.

sentences.text: The parents and relatives of the petitioner are abetted the petitioner for commission of offence.
After registering the FIR for the offences punishable under Section 366 (A) and 109 of IPC, the petitioner was arrested on 01.07.2022 and he is in judicial custody.
The police after investigating the case has filed the charge-sheet.
The petitioner moved the bail petition before the learned Sessions Judge, which came to be rejected.
Hence, the petitioner is before this Court.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in judicial custody for more than one year and 04 months.
The evidence of the PW.1 - prosecutrix is already completed.
Even the complainant has also examined and there is contradiction in their evidence, which does not believe at this stage.
The FSL report reveals that there is no seminal stains on the victim.
The story of the prosecution cannot be believable, where the accused kept the victim for 09 days in the open land without food, water and shelter.
She has stated before the Doctor that there was a love affair, which was suppressed in the Court.
The material witnesses are already examined.
Hence, prayed for allowing the petition.

05. Per contra, the learned Addl. SPP. seriously objected the petition and contended that though there is 02 days delay in lodging the complaint, that cannot be a ground for granting the bail, by disbelieving the statement of the complainant, as they are searched the victim and later they have filed the complaint.
The case is under trial NC: 2023:KHC-K:8664 and the Court cannot disbelieve the evidence of the witnesses still more material witnesses to be examined by the prosecution.
At this stage, if the bail is granted, there is possibility of tampering the witnesses and absconding from the case, which cannot be ruled out.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

06. Having heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the records it reveals that it is undisputed fact that the complaint was lodged against five persons including the parents of the petitioner and relatives for abducting the minor girl for compelling her marriage.
The offence punishable under Section 366(A) and 109 of IPC for abatement.

During the investigation the Investigating Officer has filed the charge- sheet against this petitioner by dropping the charges against other accused persons, which is also under Section 109 read with Section 34 of IPC.

In the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. and also in the evidence, the victim has stated that the petitioner was insisting her for NC: 2023:KHC-K:8664 marriage and he has forcibly taken her in his motorcycle and kept her in land behind the Temple for 09 days.
During that time, he has sexually assaulted for three times on her and threaten her with dire consequences.

07. Though, the learned counsel for the petitioner trying to elicit in the cross-examination that for 09 days they are stayed together in a open land without food and water, it is not possible to stay without food and water.
There is a contradiction in the evidence of the victim, but the same cannot be looked into while considering the bail application, as the matter is under trial.
However, the PW.1 - victim has already examined in toto and she has supported the case of the prosecution.
The father of the complainant has also examined as PW.2 and he has also supported the case of the prosecution.
Now, only the circumstantial witnesses are left out for the purpose of examination.

sentences.text: The material witnesses are already examined by the prosecution.
The FSL report NC: 2023:KHC-K:8664 reveals that there is no seminal stains detected and the medical report also reveals that there is no recent sexual intercourse on the victim.
The victim has stated before the Doctor that there is a love affair between them.
08. The petitioner is in judicial custody for more than one year and four months.
The material witnesses are already examined, except the official witnesses and other circumstantial witnesses.
Considering the same, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, by imposing certain conditions if bail is granted to the petitioner, no prejudice would be caused to the prosecution.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
